question: Name CBA's FY26 notable and restructuring items, quantify them in total, and state their effect on operating expense growth and the cost-to-income ratio (headline vs underlying).
answer: CBA's FY26 restructuring and notable items total $170 million (cash basis), comprising NZ legal settlements, ASIC Better Banking goodwill payments, and domestic customer remediation [ev-1, ev-2]. These items are excluded from underlying metrics. Underlying operating expenses grew 6% to $13,585 million [ev-5], while headline operating expenses (including the $170m items) grew 5.8% [ev-9]. The underlying cost-to-income ratio increased by 30 basis points to 45.2% [ev-11], contrasting with a 30 bps decrease in the narrative which appears inconsistent with the table data [ev-6 vs ev-11]. The headline cost-to-income ratio improved by 20 basis points to 45.5% [ev-7].
